messages:
laura: Quick heads-up — I'm opening a tiny PR to tidy the 'hello-dock' quickstart. Main goals: make the auth section clearer (env vs file), fix the Dockerfile example, and add a short note about not committing creds. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4321

aj: Nice, will take a look in a bit. Is this mostly copy edits or are you changing sample code too?

laura: Both. Copy + tiny snippet swap. I replaced the old inline token with an .env usage example and swapped the Dockerfile to a multi-stage build so image size is smaller. Kept the app code identical.

kevin: Can you paste the new Dockerfile here? Quick scan first.

laura: Sure — pasted below:

```dockerfile
# stage 1: build
FROM python:3.11-slim AS builder
WORKDIR /build
COPY pyproject.toml requirements.txt ./
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt -t /build/.deps

# stage 2: runtime
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder /build/.deps /app/.deps
COPY . /app
ENV PYTHONPATH=/app/.deps:/app
CMD ["python", "app.py"]
```

mike: That looks good. Two small asks: 1) add a comment to the auth section showing how to use the env var locally (`export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...`) and 2) show the minimal .env file example — some folks copy/paste creds by accident.

laura: Yep — included both. Draft text: "Create a .env file (do not commit) with REDWOOD_API_KEY=your_token_here and load it with direnv or python-dotenv for local testing."

kevin: Suggestion: add a quick warning snippet for CI: `echo \"$REDWOOD_API_KEY\" | gh secret set REDWOOD_API_KEY` or similar so users know how to set it in GH Actions.

laura: Good call — I'll add a one-liner for GitHub Actions secrets and a minimal workflow example referencing the quickstart.

aj: On the examples front, can we keep the SDK call as the newest stable method? We had a deprecation in SDK 5 -> 6 earlier; I don't want this to reintroduce older patterns. Which function are you using?

laura: Using `client.generate()` from the SDK wrapper — that's the recommended path in our current SDK. I tested locally against a mock.

kevin: Docsbot run link-check? (docsbot is a CI helper)

docsbot: Running link-check on changed files... Found 1 broken internal link in docs/quickstarts/hello-dock.md: ./old-auth.md -> should be ../auth/setup.md

laura: Thanks — patched that in the PR.

mike: I skimmed the language around rate limits. Could we add a callout: "If you expect >10 req/s, consider Dedicated or batch settings" — just a pointer to infra options with a link to the dedicated page.

laura: Will add a short aside and link to /docs/dedicated/overview.

aj: I'll do a quick review now and flag anything blocking. If all good, we can merge and cherry-pick to the v-next branch.

kevin: +1 from me as long as sample commands don't print tokens to stdout (e.g., avoid `echo $TOKEN` unguarded).

laura: Updated — replaced any risky examples with `printf '***'` placeholders. Also added a tiny troubleshooting blurb for Docker networking (if localhost:3000 doesn't connect, use host networking on macos with `--network=host`).

mike: Awesome. Minor nit: add `COPY --chown=1000:1000` in runtime stage for best practices (non-root). Optional though.

laura: Added it and ran a local build quick smoke. Build log: `Successfully built image hello-dock:local (size 82MB)` — added that as proof in the PR description.

aj: Reviewed, left two inline comments about wording. Nothing functional.

laura: Thanks all — I'll address comments and merge after CI passes. If anyone wants final tweaks, ping me here. :rocket:
